cf.title: Let OpenSSL auto-select DH parameters by default

input.subject: Let OpenSSL auto-select DH parameters by default

verdict_reasoning: One objection survived, security-1, and it is fixable. A server with a key below 2048 bits and an empty ssl_dh_params_file loses the 2048-bit DH floor on upgrade, with no warning or release note. The goal and the design are otherwise sound, and no level fails. Someone who knows the OpenSSL code must confirm the library behavior and the version coverage.

brief.title: Let OpenSSL auto-select DH parameters when ssl_dh_params_file is unset
brief.problem: The server falls back to the compiled-in FILE_DH2048 parameters when ssl_dh_params_file is empty, and nobody knows when or how to update them. The author wants the parameter size to follow the server key size and current practice without manual upkeep.
brief.proposed_design: When ssl_dh_params_file is empty, the server calls SSL_CTX_set_dh_auto() so OpenSSL picks well-known parameters sized to the certificate key, and FILE_DH2048 goes away. The docs mark ssl_dh_params_file as obsolescent and README.SSL loses its ephemeral DH section. A failed DH file load on reload now fails the reload and keeps the old SSL context, where before it fell back to built-in parameters.
user_visible_surface: ssl_dh_params_file: the empty default now means library-chosen DH parameters, and the docs call the setting obsolescent.
Reload behavior: an unreadable ssl_dh_params_file now fails the SSL reload and keeps the old context instead of using built-in parameters.
Servers with small keys may get DH parameters smaller than the old 2048-bit default.
author_claims: SSL_CTX_set_dh_auto() exists in all relevant OpenSSL and LibreSSL versions.
Auto-selected parameter size grows with key size and future standards.
The OpenSSL documentation recommends this approach.
The old reload fallback to built-in parameters was a bug.
Smaller DH parameters only occur with key sizes that ignore current best practice.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. The entry has moved through two CommitFests with no recorded review.
unclear: The material does not name the minimum OpenSSL and LibreSSL versions that support SSL_CTX_set_dh_auto(), or how they compare to the supported minimum.
The material does not say what sizes OpenSSL picks for common key types such as RSA 2048 or ECDSA keys.
The material does not say whether the reload behavior change is meant for back-patching or gets a release note.
The material does not say whether removing the FILE_DH2048 macro from libpq-be.h affects extensions.
The material does not say whether the old ssldump advice in README.SSL still applies or has a replacement.

objections.title: Silent drop below 2048-bit DH for servers with small keys
objections.failure_scenario: A site runs an old 1024-bit RSA certificate and upgrades Postgres. With the empty default, SSL_CTX_set_dh_auto() picks DH parameters matched to that key, so TLS 1.2 DHE sessions use a smaller group than the old 2048-bit built-in one. Nothing in the server log or the docs tells the administrator.
objections.argument: Message #1 accepts that small keys can now give DH parameters below the old default, and calls that the user's own fault. Today the compiled-in parameters set a 2048-bit floor for DHE sessions, whatever the certificate size. The patch removes that floor on upgrade, with no setting change, no warning and no planned release note. OpenSSL security levels may reject such keys on some builds, but the proposal does not rely on that or say which builds do.
objections.author_must_show: Why not keep a 2048-bit minimum, for example by logging a warning or refusing auto-selected groups below it, and will the release notes mention the change?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 confirms the drop and proposes no warning, floor or release note. The affected case is narrow (small keys, TLS 1.2 DHE ciphers only), but a server upgraded with unchanged settings does lose the 2048-bit floor, so it stays fixable.

refuted.title: Existing servers may silently negotiate smaller DH parameters after upgrade
refuted.failure_scenario: A site keeps an old 1024-bit RSA certificate and leaves ssl_dh_params_file empty. After a major upgrade, TLS 1.2 DHE sessions use smaller DH parameters than the old 2048-bit built-in set, with no log message. The site learns of it from an external TLS scanner or a compliance audit.
refuted.argument: Message #1 accepts that small keys now get DH parameters below the old 2048-bit default. The proposal treats this as acceptable because such keys ignore best practice. That reasoning may hold, but the change still reaches users who changed nothing in their configuration. The material adds no floor, no warning, and no release-note text for this case.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the release notes or a server warning tell users with keys smaller than 2048 bits that their DH parameter size can drop after upgrade?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of security-1. Both describe the same 1024-bit RSA upgrade case, and security-1 states the lost 2048-bit floor more exactly and fits the safety item better than item 6.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch removes the FILE_DH2048 macro from src/include/libpq/libpq-be.h, a backend header that extensions can include.

touch_points.label: new GUC
touch_points.reason: No new GUC, but the empty default of ssl_dh_params_file changes meaning and the docs mark the setting obsolescent.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The patch changes which DH parameters TLS 1.2 DHE sessions use, and small keys can get groups below 2048 bits.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #1 calls the old reload fallback a bug but does not say whether that fix is meant for back branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch removes compiled-in parameters that had no update process and makes the server depend on SSL_CTX_set_dh_auto() in OpenSSL and LibreSSL.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why not keep a 2048-bit minimum for auto-selected DH parameters, or log a warning when the selected group is smaller?
What DH parameter sizes does SSL_CTX_set_dh_auto() pick for RSA 2048, RSA 3072 and ECDSA P-256 server keys?
Which OpenSSL and LibreSSL versions first provide SSL_CTX_set_dh_auto(), and are they at or below the minimum versions Postgres supports?
Is the reload behavior change for an unreadable ssl_dh_params_file meant for back-patching, and will it get a release note?
Does any known extension use the FILE_DH2048 macro from libpq-be.h?

committability.owner_note: Peter Eisentraut, a committer per the review notes, wrote the patch. A second reviewer who knows the OpenSSL backend code and LibreSSL differences has not spoken in the thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the default TLS 1.2 DHE parameters of every server with an empty ssl_dh_params_file, and for future changes in how OpenSSL and LibreSSL pick them. This lasts as long as TLS 1.2 is supported.
committability.author_follow_up: The author moved the entry to the next CommitFest on 2026-10-01 and asked for reviews in message #1.

priority.reason: The change affects every server that leaves ssl_dh_params_file empty, which is the default, and it removes compiled-in parameters that nobody knew how to update. The patch is about 9 KiB in one backend file plus docs, with one fixable point (security-1) to settle.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody can confirm that a failed DH file load on reload keeps the old SSL context, or how the patch behaves on LibreSSL. The sizes OpenSSL picks for common key types were also not checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: DSA Hash Tables (DHT): hash tables backed by DSM segments
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a general-purpose hash table in DSA memory, so several backends can share it and it can grow, along the lines of dynahash. It uses separate chaining, incremental resizing, partition-based locking and concurrent iteration.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author parked the patch after its only planned user, Dilip Kumar's Parallel Bitmap Heap Scan, stopped using it. He did not expect a committer to take it without a concrete user, which Andres Freund had asked for at the start. Reviewers found no problems with the design.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Since Dilip Kumar's Parallel Bitmap Heap Scan project is no longer using this, I think I should park it here unless/until another potential use case pops up.

precedents_retrieved.title: Direct SSL Connections
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the server accept a standard TLS handshake directly as the first bytes of a connection, without the SSLRequest round trip, and adds a libpq connection parameter (sslnegotiation=direct) for clients to use it. Later versions add ALPN with a placeholder protocol name and allow pipelining the ClientHello after SSLRequest.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show a final decision. The last messages, from July 2023, are review comments that ask for changes: make ALPN mandatory for direct SSL connections, drop the sslalpn option, move the buffered-data handling into secure_open_server(), and fix a static buffer in PQsslAttribute that is not thread-safe. No later patch version or author reply is shown before the entry was returned with feedback in December 2023.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add test case for sslinfo
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Thomas Munro, Michael Paquier, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a regression test suite for contrib/sslinfo, using a bash script that copies certificates into $PGDATA and restarts the server with a custom configuration. It ships its own set of SSL certificates.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for a different design. They wanted the tests built on src/test/ssl/ as TAP tests, with the existing certificates and no fixed expected output, since TLS versions and ciphers differ between installations. The patch also required bash and assumed PGDATA was set, so it failed on cfbot. The author did not answer the September request for an updated version.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think sslinfo should be tested as an extension of src/test/ssl/
instead of its own test suite.  There are too many complications that we
would otherwise have to solve again.

precedents_retrieved.title: Set host(no)ssl settings from initdb
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add initdb options (--auth-hostssl, --auth-hostnossl, later also GSS variants) that write hostssl/hostnossl lines with a chosen auth method into the generated pg_hba.conf. The goal is to let users reject non-TLS remote connections without editing pg_hba.conf by hand after initdb.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying and the author sent no rebase for two months, so Michael Paquier returned it. He also doubted that initdb should carry this logic and pointed to a server-side sslmode=require as a possible alternative. Earlier, Tom Lane said most users run initdb through vendor packaging scripts, so a new option does not help unless vendors pass it through.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I agree that
being able to reject easily non-SSL connections in pg_hba.conf is a
bit of a hassle now, but putting more logic into initdb does not seem
the right course to me.

precedents_retrieved.title: Opclass parameters
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds per-column opclass parameters to create index, stored as serialized reloptions in a new pg_index.indoptions column and passed to GiST and GIN support functions through a new amopclassoptions routine. Follow-up patches add a 'siglen' parameter to several GiST opclasses (tsvector_ops, intarray, ltree, pg_trgm, hstore) and 'numranges' to gist__int_ops.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch arrived at the last moment for the final PG11 commitfest with no prior discussion, and David Steele judged it too large for that commitfest. Nikolay Shaplov objected that it splits options into global and local ones instead of building on his pending reloptions API refactoring, and that the parameters belong in pg_attribute.attoptions instead of a new pg_index column. Oleg Bartunov, on the author's side, agreed to Returned with Feedback so the storage and syntax could be discussed on -hackers.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In addition, based on Nikolay's response, I think the patch should be
marked Returned with Feedback until it is reconciled with the existing
patches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Opclass parameters
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds per-column opclass parameters to create index, such as `gist__intbig_ops (siglen = 32)`, stored per index column and parsed by an opclass support function. Later versions made this generic for all access methods through support function 0 and added an `amattoptions()` method for per-column AM options.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra objected to the September 2019 design: support function number 0 breaks the procnum convention, and passing parsed options through FmgrInfo.fn_expr misuses a field meant for the call's parse tree. He also found a bug in identify_opfamily_groups() with procnum 0. The author did not address this review in the seven weeks before Michael Paquier closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The latest review has not been addressed, and this was 7 weeks ago.

precedents_retrieved.title: Simplify ExecWithoutOverlapsNotEmpty by removing unused parameter
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the unused atttypid parameter from the static function ExecWithoutOverlapsNotEmpty(). It also replaces a lookup_type_cache() call, made only to read typtype, with get_typtype().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Two reviewers approved the patch, and Chao Li noted that get_typtype() returns '\0' instead of raising an error for an invalid type OID, which changes the error message. No message shows the author answering or withdrawing the patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix incorrect Spanish translation and remove obsolete FIXME comments in es.po
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch corrects one message in src/backend/po/es.po that translated "physical replication slot" as logical replication. It also removes several FIXME translator comments in that file that the author judged obsolete.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Translation fixes belong on the pgsql-translators mailing list, not on pgsql-hackers or in the commitfest. The entry was withdrawn after reviewers pointed this out, and the thread does not discuss the patch content.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Thanks for your submission, all translation related fixes should be posted to
the pgsql-translators@ mailinglist.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no row about the same or a similar idea, and message #1 does not point to an earlier discussion of auto-selected DH parameters. From the prior-attempts angle there is no earlier rejection reason to carry over.
The reload change aligns DH file errors with other SSL reload errors and is safe. Marking the GUC obsolescent without removing it keeps existing configs and dumps working.

From the replication and on-disk angle, I have no objection. The proposal touches no on-disk format, WAL, catalog or Postgres protocol message; it only changes how the server picks TLS 1.2 DH parameters at SSL context setup. A walsender or other client that negotiates TLS 1.2 gets library-chosen parameters, but the protocol is unchanged. The removed FILE_DH2048 macro is a backend-internal constant in a new major version, so I see no realistic extension ABI break.

Only one security point found. The reload change, which keeps the old SSL context when the DH file cannot be loaded, is safer than the old fallback. Preferring well-known groups matches current TLS practice, so neither is raised.

From the maintenance and fit angle, the proposal lowers long-run cost. It removes the compiled-in FILE_DH2048 parameters, which nobody knew when or how to update, and hands sizing to the TLS library. It adds no GUC, no hot-path cost and no new dependency, and a committer wrote it. Points that need the code or more information: the oldest OpenSSL and LibreSSL versions that have SSL_CTX_set_dh_auto(), whether any extension uses FILE_DH2048, and whether the reload change gets a release note. No reviewer engaged in two CommitFests, which bears on committability, not on the merits.

Postgres has no existing way to make the default DH parameters track key size without manual upkeep. ssl_dh_params_file needs each administrator to supply a file, and the patch replaces Postgres's own compiled-in parameters with the SSL library's mechanism, so it removes a mechanism and adds none.

No demand objection applies. The patch removes code, the compiled-in FILE_DH2048 parameters, that has no documented process for keeping it current, and it adds no feature, GUC, syntax or catalog surface that needs a user group to justify it. The benefit goes to every server that leaves ssl_dh_params_file empty, which is the default, so the users who gain are the same users who carry any risk. The open points are the small-key DH size, the reload behavior change, the minimum OpenSSL and LibreSSL versions, and removing the libpq-be.h macro. These are safety and compatibility questions for other angles.
